label: text
text: Many people who read Mr. Churchill's statement that the Act prohibiting the export of gold coin or bullion was to be repealed may be under the impression that gold has not been exported from Britain since 1919 when the Act was passed, says the "Daily Chronicle."

label: text
text: Nothing could be further from reality. During the last five years gold has been among the chief exports of this country, under Government licence.

label: text
text: In 1920 re exported 92% of the world's pounds' worth of gold; in 1921, 59 millions; in 1922, nearly 45 millions; in 1923, over 57 millions; and last year, close on 50 millions — a total of about 303 millions.

label: text
text: The greater part of this, no less than 177 millions, went to the United States to pay our debts. The rest, 49 millions were shipped to India, which always make a heavy demand on our resource.

label: text
text: Whence comes the gold which we scatter so freely? Mainly from South Africa; the greater part from the Transva'th though Rhodesia is a steady contributor of about £2,000,000 a year. And there are windfalls unex- mined in the official returns. For example, France sent us £710,799 in 1920.

label: text
text: But on balance we have patted with nearly 9 million of gold in the last five years, and it is consulting to knc from the Chancellor of the Exerer that our accumulated reserve is as high as 153 million.

label: text
text: Rats are a change has come over the scene during the first three months of the present year. We have exported £11,636,685 in gold and imported £8,542,548. But of the imports the surprising thing is that £4,246,000 come from the United States.

label: text
text: There is another interesting feature about the Board of Trade Returns. At the end of last year we exported over £2,000,000 in gold bars to Russia, the first transaction of the kind for a very long time.

label: text
text: Already this year we have sent another £342,111 in gold bullion or Russia. Russia is a large place, and it is not all under the Soviet Government, so probably there is a simple explanation.

label: text
text: There is, at any rate, no indication in the imports of any Bolshevik gold coming to this country in a solid form.

label: text
text: Travellers tell us that Great Britain is about the only place in the world now in which it is difficult to come by an English sovereign. We have been broadcasting them for a long time past. Should you travel in Albania, you will find the sovereign well represented in the very much mixed coinage of that country. Among the Arabs on the shores of the Red Sea the sovereign is a familiar and highly-prized coin. Already this year two and a half millions have gone to India.

label: text
text: It is, perhaps, the best advertisement this country could have, for the sovereign is always "worth its weight in gold" and can now hold its head up, even in the company of dollars.

text: MR. RUNCIMAN ON THE DANGERS OF NATIONALISATION.

label: text
text: "Those who are conducting the campaign in favour of what they call nationalising the banks should understand that the banks are owned, not by a few rich men, but by an immense number of individual shareholders, and that the average holding is remarkably small."

label: text
text: This is a passage from a letter which Mr. Walter Runciman, director of the Westmioster Bank, has sent to "The Daily Chronicle," with reference to proposals at the recent I.L.P. conference for the nationalisation of the banks.

label: text
text: Mr. Runciman gives the following figures of five big banks:—Barclays.—Capital, £15,592,372; 51.011 shareholders; average holding, £306.

According to preliminary figures Manitoba will show about 2,643,000 acres this year, skatchewan, 8,555,183, and Albion, 2,721,689, making a total of 3,919,872, which compares with 14,153,905 in 1923. label: text
text: Toronto, Ontario.—The construction of the Ontario Hydro-Electric Commission's proposed steam auxiliary power, coking and heating plant will be proceeded with this summer, according to an opinion expressed by Mayor Foster, of this city. It is proposed at this plant to develop 100,000 horsepower of electricity. In addition the plant will produce 13,500,000 cubic feet of gas, and coal to the amount of 1,930 tons carbonized daily would produce coke to the amount of 1,353 tons a day. As it is estimated the plant would use 500,000 tons of coal a year, this would mean 493,845 tons of coke a year, or a little more than half of Toronto's domestic demand of anthracite per annum.

label: text
text: Edmonton, Alberta.—Acquiring the tract of 260,000 acres of land holdings of the Western Canada Land Company, originally purchased from the Canadian Pacific Railway, the British Land Settlement Corporation plans a great colonization scheme for central and northern Alberta. The lands in question stretch across the province north of Edmonton from the district north of Vermilion to Wasamum. It is intended to bring out large groups of immigrants, who will receive financial assistance.

label: text
text: Vancouver, British Columbia. Expenditure of a sum in the neighbourhood of $1,000,000 in the rearrangement of the local plant of the Vancouver Lumber Company, Limited, and in practically doubling the capacity of the mill, is to be made following the purchase of that concern by a syndicate of American lumber men.

label: text
text: Victoria, British Columbia.—Official figures relating to the 1924 mineral production in British Columbia show that the output totalled $48,621,007, an increase over 1923 of $7,316,777, or 176 per cent. Placer gold production in 1924 amounted to 21,037 ounces; lode gold, 233,142 ounces; silver, 8,341,169 ounces; copper, 64,393 pounds; lead, 170,384,481 pounds; zinc, 79,130,970 pounds.

label: text
text: The directors of Allenby Rubber Co., in their report for the twelve months ended February 28, last state that the net profit for the period after making due provision for depreciation was $44,255.38, to which has to be added the balance of $26,756.65 brought forward from last account making a total of $71,012.03. After deducting the interim dividend of 5 per cent. paid on January 10, 1925, there remains a balance of $55,308.74 available as at February 28, 1925. The directors recommend that a final dividend of 10 per cent. be paid for the year, absorbing $31,405.58. The total distribution of 15 per cent. is very slightly more than the profit earned, but with improved prospects and the redemption of the debenture being fully provided for the directors feel quite justified in drawing slightly on the large balance which in very different circumstances was carried forward a year ago.

label: text
text: One of the greatest mystery plays of the year was "The Roar Car" by Edward Rose. The play ran for a long period at the Majestic Theatre in Los Angeles with Richard Bonnett in the role of "crime defector." It was so successful that it was immediately taken back. Many were of the opinion that it was the best mystery play since "The Bat." The Goldwyn company made the screen version of this mystifying piece "Red Lights" as the screen version is called, and has in the east many of the screen's best artists including Raymond Griffith, Marie Prevost, Jimmy Walker, Alice Lake and others. Raymond Griffith assumed the role of the crime defector.

label: text
text: In "Red Lights" which is coming to the World Theatre on Wednesday next for a four days' run, the mysterious complications keep a tense interest throughout, and hold the audience in a state of suspense until the very last scene. During the introduction of the stage play the end of the audience shrieked the grasped at the thrilling situations. The screen version "Red Lights" promises to present much more of a thrill as the different scenes can be made more realistic than they could possibly have been on the stage. The greater part of the action transpires in the reascar of the Continental Limited.
